_info: Ashkin raid — refugees arrive, beg for captive rescue. Player decides force size, then fights. 'Three hands' = 15, but refugees can't count well. Actually ~12 ashkin.
title: Smoke and Ashes
description: Refugees from a destroyed settlement beg for help rescuing captives from an ashkin raiding party.

arrival.text:
The rangers bring them in at dusk. Eight souls. Burned clothes, crusted blood, bare feet. Two children cling to a woman who stares at nothing.

The eldest — a man with one ear missing, fresh — drops to his knees before {chieftain}.

'They came at dawn. Grey skin, no words, just teeth. They took our people. Dragged them north. Please.'

{chieftain} asks: how many?

The man holds up both hands, then one more. Three hands. His people have no word for fifteen.

'Please. They have our children.'

choices.label: March in strength — twelve warriors. We end this.
A war-band of seven. Enough to fight, not enough to leave us open.
Three scouts. Fast, quiet. Find them before they dig in.
We cannot risk our people for strangers.

march_many.text:
Twelve warriors. Nearly every fighting body in the village. {chieftain} leads them north through the tree line.

The village gate stands open behind you. Elders, children, the healer. If anything comes from the east while you are gone...

Two days of hard march. Then smoke. A crude camp between boulders. You count them: ten. Maybe twelve. Not fifteen. The man with one ear was wrong. Or afraid.

Your twelve against their twelve. But you have iron. They have bone and rage.

combat_many.text: Dawn. Your warriors pour over the rocks. The ashkin scramble for their weapons. Too late. Too slow.

stances.label: Open — fight in the line with your men
Rearward — direct the assault from behind

rescue_total.text:
It is over in minutes. The ashkin scatter into the rocks. Your warriors find the captives in a pit behind the camp — nine souls, bound with sinew, alive. A woman clutches a boy to her chest and won't let go.

The march home takes three days. The freed captives walk among your warriors. Some of them look back at your village and weep. Not from sadness.

But for three days, the village stood open. The elder who stayed behind aged a year in each one.
rescue_total.log: Twelve warriors marched north and crushed an ashkin camp. Nine captives freed. The village stood undefended for three days.

pyrrhic_many.text:
They fought harder than anyone expected. Grey bodies hurling themselves at shield walls, biting through leather. Two of your warriors don't get up.

You find the captives. Alive. But the walk home is quiet. The freed weep with relief. Your men carry their dead.
pyrrhic_many.log: The ashkin were defeated but two warriors fell. Captives were freed. The village was left exposed.

march_medium.text:
Seven warriors. {chieftain} picks them carefully — the strongest, the steadiest. Enough to guard the village, enough to fight.

Two days north. The ashkin camp sits between boulders in a ravine. You count them from the ridge: twelve. Maybe more in the caves behind. Three hands was close.

Seven against twelve. Your iron against their fury. This will cost.

choices.label: Wait for nightfall — hit them while they sleep

combat_medium.text: First light. You spread your seven across the ravine mouth. No retreat for either side. The ashkin see you and bare their teeth. No war cry. Just silence and the scrape of bone on stone.

stances.label: Forward — break their line before they set
Open — hold formation, grind them down
Defensive — shield wall in the ravine mouth

combat_medium_night.text:
You wait. The stars come out. The ashkin sleep in shifts — two sentries by a low fire. Your men move like shadows between the boulders.

Then a stone slips under someone's foot. A sentry turns. His eyes catch the moonlight.

Now.

combat.round_1_text: Chaos in the dark. Shapes collide. Someone screams — yours or theirs, you can't tell.

stances.label: Forward — strike fast in the confusion
Open — find a target, fight steady
Rearward — use the darkness, pick them off

rescue_medium_win.text:
The last ashkin drops. Your warriors stand panting, blades red. One of your men sits against a boulder, holding his side. He'll live. Probably.

Behind the camp, in a pit covered with branches: seven captives. Thin. Bruised. Alive.

The walk home is long. The freed ones don't talk much. Neither do your warriors.
rescue_medium_win.log: Seven warriors fought the ashkin and won. Captives freed. All warriors returned, though not all unharmed.

rescue_medium_lose.text:
{chieftain} falls back. Blood in your eyes, a ringing in your skull. Your warriors drag you out.

Three made it back. Three out of seven. The captives are still in the pit. You can hear them calling as you retreat into the trees.

The village receives you in silence. The healer works through the night.
rescue_medium_lose.log: The rescue attempt failed. Three warriors lost. The ashkin tracked the survivors home.

rescue_medium_stalemate.text:
Neither side breaks. The fighting grinds to a halt as the sun climbs. Your warriors bleed. The ashkin bleed. Between the boulders, both sides watch each other.

Then the ashkin begin to withdraw. Not running — walking backward, dragging their wounded. They take the captives with them. Deeper into the hills.

You could follow. But your men are spent.
rescue_medium_stalemate.log: The battle was inconclusive. The ashkin withdrew with their captives. One warrior lost.

march_few.text:
Three scouts. The fastest, the quietest. No armour, just blades and shadows.

{chieftain} watches them leave at dusk. One of them — barely old enough to shave — looks back once.

Four days pass. Then five.

On the sixth morning, two figures stumble from the tree line. Just two. The young one is not with them.

The older scout speaks in flat tones. 'We found them. More than three hands. We freed three captives in the night, maybe four. Then they heard us. Erek...' He stops. 'Erek didn't make it out.'

Behind the two scouts, four strangers emerge from the trees. Freed captives. Eyes wide. Grateful. Broken.
march_few.log: Scouts attempted a night rescue. Four captives freed. One scout — Erek — was killed. The ashkin know where to find us.

refuse_end.text:
The one-eared man stares at {chieftain}. He does not beg again. He stands, slowly, and gathers his people.

The woman with the children looks at you. She doesn't speak. She doesn't need to.

They leave before dawn. Heading west. One of the children waves at the gate guard. The guard doesn't wave back.

At the morning council, no one mentions them. But the healer sets an extra bowl of broth on the step, just in case. It sits there all day, growing cold.
refuse_end.log: Refugees begged for help rescuing captives from the ashkin. They were turned away.
